userStories.title: DB migration — create workflow_configs table with constraints and seed rows
userStories.description: Create a new PostgreSQL migration file `20260404000001_workflow_configs.sql` that adds the `workflow_configs` table. The table stores one row per Rorca workflow (spec_generation, pipeline_execution, memory_consolidation) with runtime, provider, and model columns. CHECK constraints enforce valid workflow_id and runtime values. Three default seed rows are inserted via INSERT ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING so re-running the migration is idempotent. The `id` column uses `gen_random_uuid()` as default. `updated_at` defaults to NOW() and must be updated on every write.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration file `backend/src/db/pg-migrations/20260404000001_workflow_configs.sql` exists and uses timestamp prefix format

Table `workflow_configs` has columns: id (UUID PK, default gen_random_uuid()), workflow_id (TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE), runtime (TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'native'), provider (TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'claude-cli'), model (TEXT nullable), updated_at (TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW())
CHECK constraint on workflow_id allows only 'spec_generation', 'pipeline_execution', 'memory_consolidation'
CHECK constraint on runtime allows only 'native', 'claude', 'opencode', 'codex'

Three seed rows inserted via INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (workflow_id) DO NOTHING: spec_generation (runtime='native', provider='claude-cli'), pipeline_execution (runtime='claude', provider='claude-cli'), memory_consolidation (runtime='native', provider='claude-cli')

userStories.title: New lib workflow-config-resolver.ts — resolveWorkflowConfig with full fallback chain
userStories.description: Create `backend/src/lib/workflow-config-resolver.ts` exporting `resolveWorkflowConfig(workflowId, userId?)` that returns `Promise<ResolvedWorkflowConfig>`. The resolution chain is: (1) DB `workflow_configs` row for the given workflowId, (2) for `pipeline_execution` only, fall back to `agent_config` table values via `getActiveAgentType()` / `getActiveAgentModel()`, (3) env vars `RORCA_AGENT` / `RORCA_MODEL` / `SPEC_PROVIDER`, (4) hardcoded defaults (runtime='native' for spec_generation/memory_consolidation, runtime='claude' for pipeline_execution, provider='claude-cli', model=null). API key resolution: call `getVaultKey(userId, resolvedProvider)` → fall back to env var (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`) → null (claude-cli needs no key). Export the `ResolvedWorkflowConfig` type with fields: workflowId, runtime, provider, model, apiKey (string|null), baseUrl (string|null). Include Jest unit tests covering all fallback levels.
acceptanceCriteria: File `backend/src/lib/workflow-config-resolver.ts` exports `resolveWorkflowConfig(workflowId: string, userId?: string): Promise<ResolvedWorkflowConfig>`

ResolvedWorkflowConfig type exported with fields: workflowId (string), runtime ('native'|'claude'|'opencode'|'codex'), provider (ProviderType), model (string|null), apiKey (string|null), baseUrl (string|null)
Resolution priority is DB workflow_configs → agent_config (pipeline_execution only) → RORCA_AGENT/RORCA_MODEL/SPEC_PROVIDER env vars → hardcoded defaults
API key resolution tries vault key first via getVaultKey(userId, provider), then env var, then null — claude-cli runtime returns null apiKey without error

Jest test file `backend/src/__tests__/workflow-config-resolver.test.ts` covers: DB row found, DB row missing with env var fallback, all defaults, vault key resolution, pipeline_execution agent_config fallback

userStories.title: New route workflow-router.ts — GET/PUT/resolved endpoints
userStories.description: Create `backend/src/routes/workflow-router.ts` with three endpoints: (1) `GET /api/workflow-router` — returns all 3 workflow_configs rows joined with vault key status (hasKey boolean per provider, masked key preview), (2) `PUT /api/workflow-router/:workflowId` — upserts a single workflow_configs row with Zod validation (validates workflowId is one of the 3 allowed values, validates runtime constraints — spec_generation and memory_consolidation must be 'native', pipeline_execution can be any runtime), (3) `GET /api/workflow-router/resolved/:workflowId` — calls `resolveWorkflowConfig()` and returns the fully resolved config with the API key masked (first 4 + last 4 chars only). All endpoints have `@swagger` JSDoc annotations. Register the router in `server.ts` at `/api/workflow-router`.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/workflow-router returns array of 3 objects with fields: workflowId, runtime, provider, model, hasApiKey (boolean), updatedAt

PUT /api/workflow-router/:workflowId accepts body { runtime?, provider?, model? }, validates via Zod, upserts to workflow_configs, returns updated row — rejects runtime != 'native' for spec_generation and memory_consolidation with 422
GET /api/workflow-router/resolved/:workflowId returns ResolvedWorkflowConfig with apiKey masked (e.g. 'sk-a...xyz9') or null if no key
Router mounted in server.ts at app.use('/api/workflow-router', workflowRouterRouter) with import added at top
All three endpoints have @swagger JSDoc annotations with request/response schemas

userStories.title: Startup seeding — ensurePersistedConfig seeds workflow_configs from agent_config
userStories.description: Modify `ensurePersistedConfig()` in `backend/src/routes/config.ts` to also seed the `workflow_configs` table from the existing `agent_config` row. After loading `agent_config` values into `currentAgentType` and `currentAgentModel`, execute an INSERT INTO workflow_configs for the `pipeline_execution` row using the loaded agentType as runtime and agentModel as model, with ON CONFLICT (workflow_id) DO NOTHING so it only seeds on first run. This ensures existing users who already have an agent_config row get their pipeline_execution workflow_config seeded without any manual migration step.
acceptanceCriteria: ensurePersistedConfig() in config.ts now inserts into workflow_configs (workflow_id, runtime, provider, model) VALUES ('pipeline_execution', $agentType, providerForRuntime($agentType), $agentModel) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
The provider value is derived from the runtime: 'claude' → 'claude-cli', 'opencode' → resolved from model registry, 'codex' → 'claude-cli'
Existing agent_config values are preserved — no destructive changes to agent_config table
If workflow_configs already has a pipeline_execution row (from migration seed), the INSERT is skipped via ON CONFLICT

userStories.title: Dual-write — PUT /api/config/agent also upserts workflow_configs pipeline_execution row
userStories.description: Modify the `PUT /api/config/agent` handler in `backend/src/routes/config.ts` to dual-write: after updating `agent_config`, also upsert the `workflow_configs` row for `pipeline_execution` with the same runtime and model values. This ensures backward compatibility — existing UI that calls PUT /api/config/agent still updates the new workflow_configs table. The upsert uses ON CONFLICT (workflow_id) DO UPDATE SET runtime=EXCLUDED.runtime, model=EXCLUDED.model, updated_at=NOW().
acceptanceCriteria: PUT /api/config/agent handler now also executes INSERT INTO workflow_configs ... ON CONFLICT (workflow_id) DO UPDATE for the 'pipeline_execution' row
The runtime value maps from agentType: 'claude' → 'claude', 'opencode' → 'opencode', 'codex' → 'codex'
The model value is the agentModel from the request body
Both writes (agent_config + workflow_configs) happen in the same request — if one fails the response returns 500

userStories.title: Migrate pipeline.ts trigger to use resolveWorkflowConfig for runtime + model + vault key
userStories.description: Modify the pipeline trigger handler in `backend/src/routes/pipeline.ts` to replace the current inline runtime/model resolution logic with a call to `resolveWorkflowConfig('pipeline_execution', userId)`. Currently the trigger resolves agent type via `RORCA_AGENT` env var → default 'claude', and model via `RORCA_MODEL` env var → spec-level model → L3 preferred_model. Replace this with: `const wfConfig = await resolveWorkflowConfig('pipeline_execution')`. Use `wfConfig.runtime` as the agent type, `wfConfig.model` as the model (still allowing per-spec model override from specJson.model to take precedence), and `wfConfig.apiKey` for vault key injection into the subprocess env. The spec-level model override chain is preserved: request body agentOverride > specJson.model > wfConfig.model.
acceptanceCriteria: pipeline.ts trigger handler calls resolveWorkflowConfig('pipeline_execution') instead of reading RORCA_AGENT/RORCA_MODEL env vars directly
Agent type (runtime) comes from wfConfig.runtime, replacing the getActiveAgentType() call and RORCA_AGENT env var check
Model resolution chain is preserved: request body model override > specJson.model > wfConfig.model > null
Vault API key from wfConfig.apiKey is injected into subprocess env vars (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / OPENROUTER_API_KEY / OPENAI_API_KEY depending on provider)
Existing agentOverride in request body still takes priority over wfConfig.runtime for backward compat

userStories.title: Migrate auto-memory.ts to use resolveWorkflowConfig('memory_consolidation')
userStories.description: Modify `autoSynthesizeMemory()` in `backend/src/lib/auto-memory.ts` to resolve its model and API key from the workflow config instead of using the hardcoded `SYNTHESIS_MODEL = 'claude-haiku-4-5-20251001'`. Call `resolveWorkflowConfig('memory_consolidation')` at the start of the function. Use `wfConfig.model` as the model (falling back to the current hardcoded haiku model if null), and pass `wfConfig.apiKey` and `wfConfig.provider` to the `chatComplete()` call via ChatOptions. This allows users to configure memory synthesis to use any provider/model.
acceptanceCriteria: autoSynthesizeMemory() calls resolveWorkflowConfig('memory_consolidation') before the chatComplete call
The model passed to chatComplete comes from wfConfig.model, falling back to 'claude-haiku-4-5-20251001' if null
The apiKey and provider from wfConfig are passed to chatComplete via ChatOptions object instead of bare model string
The hardcoded SYNTHESIS_MODEL constant is kept as a fallback default but is no longer the unconditional choice

userStories.title: Migrate specs.ts spec generation to use resolveWorkflowConfig('spec_generation')
userStories.description: Modify spec generation in `backend/src/routes/specs.ts` to use `resolveWorkflowConfig('spec_generation', userId)` instead of the inline `resolveVaultCreds()` + `SPEC_PROVIDER` env var logic. The current flow resolves model from request body → L3 preferred_model → DEFAULT_MODEL, then resolves vault creds via `resolveVaultCreds(userId, model)`. Replace with: call `resolveWorkflowConfig('spec_generation', userId)`, use its model as the default (request body model still overrides), and use its apiKey/baseUrl/provider directly. Remove the `SPEC_PROVIDER` env var usage from the spec generation code path — it remains as a fallback inside `resolveWorkflowConfig`.
acceptanceCriteria: Spec generation route handler calls resolveWorkflowConfig('spec_generation', userId) instead of resolveVaultCreds() directly
Request body model override still takes priority over wfConfig.model
The wfConfig.apiKey, wfConfig.baseUrl, and wfConfig.provider are used in the chatComplete call, replacing the inline SPEC_PROVIDER resolution
The resolveVaultCreds() function remains in specs.ts for other callers (add-stories, enrich) but is no longer used in the main generate flow

userStories.title: Frontend ConnectionsHubSection component — one card per connection with status and key management
userStories.description: Create a new React component `ConnectionsHubSection` in `src/panels/settings/ProviderSettingsTab.tsx` (or a separate file imported into it). This component replaces the current 'providers' section. It renders one card per connection type: (1) Claude CLI subscription — shows install status badge (green/amber) from GET /api/config → opencodeInstalled/codexInstalled pattern, no API key needed; (2) Anthropic API — shows vault key status dot (green if key exists, gray if not), masked key preview, add/remove button; (3) OpenRouter — same pattern as Anthropic; (4) OpenAI-Compatible — shows base URL + key status; (5) Ollama — shows base URL/port configuration. Each card has a consistent layout: icon, provider name, status dot, masked key or 'Not configured', and an action button (Add Key / Remove / Test Connection). Uses existing vault API calls (GET /api/vault/keys, POST /api/vault/keys, DELETE /api/vault/keys/:id).
acceptanceCriteria: ConnectionsHubSection renders 5 connection cards: Claude CLI, Anthropic API, OpenRouter, OpenAI-Compatible, Ollama
Each card shows a status indicator: green dot if vault key exists (from GET /api/vault/keys), gray dot if not configured
Claude CLI card shows install badge (green 'Installed' or amber 'Not found') based on GET /api/config response, no API key field
Add Key button opens an inline input that saves via POST /api/vault/keys; Remove button calls DELETE /api/vault/keys/:id with confirmation
Component fetches vault keys on mount and re-fetches after add/remove operations

userStories.title: WorkflowRouterSection runtime picker — segmented control with install badges
userStories.description: Add interactive runtime selection to the WorkflowRouterSection pipeline_execution row. userStories.title: SpecsPanel default model from workflow config — fetch resolved spec_generation config
userStories.description: Modify the spec generation flow in the SpecsPanel (Forge section) to fetch the default model from the workflow router instead of using a hardcoded default. userStories.title: Backward compat test — env vars still work as fallback when DB has default seed rows
userStories.description: Write a Jest test in `backend/src/__tests__/workflow-config-fallback.test.ts` that verifies environment variable fallback behavior.
